page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The system is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.c5.xlarge in the lower performance tiers. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core stress-ng score of 1103.19 and a multi-core score of 2934.5, both falling within the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory performance is also constrained; the passmark memory score of 1246.19 and large-block read bandwidth of 20.58 GB/sec rank in the bottom 10%. Computational tasks such as single-threaded gzip compression (19.02 GB/sec) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (14.8 GB/sec) also register in the bottom 10% to 25% performance brackets.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is structured for compute-focused workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the benchmark data indicates significant performance tradeoffs, with weak single-core and multi-core processing capabilities. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers an entry-level entry point for dedicated x86_64 compute resources, but is limited by its lack of local storage and low baseline network bandwidth. It is suitable for lightweight web serving, basic redis operations, and small-scale batch processing where high-performance throughput is not critical.
